title: Debit/Credit ledger reconciliation for cross-window overdrafts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers using reserved capacity and rolling windows have observed occasional overdrafts where usage from overlapping windows is double-applied or not credited back. These cases appear during cross-region migrations, timezone boundary resets, and transient lease reassignments. The root cause is inconsistent ledger operations during window boundary processing and failed checkpoint commits. Goal: Implement a robust debit/credit reconciliation flow that ensures ledger idempotency, provides an auditable correction path for cross-window overdrafts, and enables automated partial refunds or burst restorations for affected tenants without human intervention.
background_and_context: Current quota ledger applies per-request token debits into a sliding/epoch window and periodically snapshots a tenant's balance. When snapshotting fails or lease ownership changes mid-window, tokens can be applied to both old and new windows or never reclaimed. Existing fixes are ad hoc (manual backfills, invoice credits) and do not scale. This ticket sits alongside telemetry and snapshot reliability work (see dependencies) and should be safe to release incrementally with canaryed rollouts.
technical_design_summary: 1) Introduce a reconciliation layer that stores compensating credit records linked to original debit ids. 2) Make debits idempotent by attaching deterministic debit_id derived from request metadata and tenant epoch. 3) On snapshot/lease transitions, compute a reconciliation delta by comparing persisted debits across window boundaries and emit compensating credits for duplicates. 4) Persist reconciliation operations in an append-only correction ledger with traceable parent_debit references and event hashes. 5) Add a retroactive backfill job that runs for a configurable horizon and can be throttled per-tenant. 6) Expose a "reconciliation audit" API and dashboard to display before/after balances and applied corrections.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No customer-facing double-charges in canary environment for a 7-day window under synthetic cross-region migration traffic. 2) All reconciliation operations are idempotent and have an audit record with debit_id, correction_id, operator, and timestamp. 3) Backfill tool can reprocess 30 days of history and produce a deterministic set of correction records. 4) Automated corrections can be disabled per-tenant. 5) Unit and integration tests covering lease handoff, snapshot commit failures, partial network partition, and DST boundary edge cases.
work_items: Design correction ledger schema and API (db migration reversible)
Add deterministic debit_id generation in meter pipeline
Implement reconciliation worker that compares overlapping windows
Add backfill command with dry-run mode and reconciliation report
Instrument telemetry and dashboards for correction volume and latency
Add RBAC flag in console to toggle auto-correction per-tenant
Write unit/integration tests and chaos test scenario
progress_updates: 2026-01-18: Discovery complete. Collected sample incidents from billing team (3 tenants) and reproduced overlapping-window double-apply with local simulator.
2026-01-25: Prototype deterministic debit_id in meter pipeline. Found one place where request replay lacked stable nonce; fixed upstream SDK instrumentation.
2026-01-30: Drafted correction ledger schema in PRD and circulated to Billing and Infra for feedback.
2026-02-04: Implemented reconciliation worker skeleton and end-to-end test harness. First run produced expected compensating credits in staging for synthetic overlap cases.
2026-02-09: Instrumented telemetry and added dashboard panels for "corrections_per_hour" and "avg_correction_latency". Canary scheduled for 5% of traffic next week.
decision_log: 2026-01-22: Chose append-only correction ledger over in-place balance mutation to preserve auditability.
2026-01-27: Agreed to use deterministic debit_id using sha1(request_id + tenant_id + window_epoch) to support idempotence across retries.
2026-02-02: Opted for eventual automatic corrections with per-tenant opt-out flag rather than manual only, to reduce mean time to remediation for high-impact tenants.
2026-02-08: Rollout strategy agreed: start with 5% canary, ramp to 25% after 48h if no errors, full rollout after 7d with backfill run complete.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Append-only corrections increase storage and query costs; mitigated by TTL and compacted daily rollups of correction summaries.
Automatic corrections could mask upstream billing engine bugs; mitigation: keep detailed audit UI and require a secondary sign-off for corrections that exceed a threshold (e.g., > $1k).
"Potential race during concurrent reconciliation runs across regions" mitigated by distributed lease and a per-tenant last_reconciliation_token to fence concurrent workers.
Backfill can generate a burst of corrections; restrict backfill concurrency per-tenant and add rate-limit to avoid downstream billing spikes.
test_plan: Unit tests for debit_id generation and ledger write idempotency
Integration test: simulate lease handoff mid-request and verify single debit and compensating credit semantics
Chaos test: network partition between meter producer and ledger consumer, simulate replay and ensure no duplicate net debit
E2E staging canary with synthetic traffic matching production traffic patterns including timezone shifts and reserved capacity bursts
Backfill dry-run validation and sample reconciliation reports for billing team signoff
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy reconciliation worker in passive mode (generate but do not apply corrections) to 100% staging and 5% production traffic for 48h. Phase 2: Enable auto-apply for canary tenants (5%). Run backfill dry-run for last 30 days. Phase 3: Ramp to 25% after 48h, review correction volumes and invoices. Phase 4: Full rollout and run full backfill for tenants in affected cohorts. Provide rollback flag to disable auto-apply and a script to revert manual credits if needed.
monitoring_and_alerts: Add SLOs: corrections_per_minute spikes, backfill_error_rate, reconciliation_worker_lag. Create PagerDuty playbook for >100 corrections/hour for any single tenant and for backfill job failures. Add Console dashboard tile with sample correction transcripts and link to tenant invoice adjustments.
operational_playbook: Runbook: How to triage a correction alert. Steps: 1) Identify tenant and correction IDs from dashboard. 2) Run reconciliation audit API for last 72h. 3) If misapplied, seed rollback via correction-revert command and open billing adjustment ticket. 4) If systemic, toggle auto-apply off and notify Billing + Customer Success.
